output.summary: The evidence supports quota-induced gaming as the main driver of backlog growth. First-contact demand rose only 4% (E3), while agent-created splits rose from 240 to 3,710 per month, and reopens rose from about 6% to 23%. The reopen rise is real, not a configuration artifact (E14). Quick-win picking rose and oldest-first picking fell after the quota (E6, E7, E15). Capacity was flat and closes per agent-day rose (E2, E10), so the effort and capacity explanations are contradicted. The backlog grew from July, before the Payroll launch on 18 August (E2, E12), so Payroll is not the main cause. Recommended next steps: suspend the per-agent quota (A3) and jointly classify the 430 aged complex tickets (A4). Do not raise the quota (A1), and do not commit the 12 hires yet (A2). The Engineering-bug contribution (H6) remains unknown.
